LESSON: VIRTUES: MANNERS OF WALKING ROAD SAFETY USE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Akhlaq 5.2 Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment (4 Lessons) By the end of the
Topic 5.3: Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use, part of Akhlaq 5.2 Virtues: Islamic clothing and adornment (4 Lessons) By the end of the in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to uphold the Islamic manners of walking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the Islamic manners of walking to uphold Islamic teachings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. assess the significance of Islamic manners of walking to promote civility,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. practise the Islamic manners of walking in day-to-day life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. recognise the Islamic manners of walking as part of Islamic ethics.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the Islamic manners of walking to uphold Islamic teachings,

   Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. assess the significance of Islamic manners of walking to promote civility,

   Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. practise the Islamic manners of walking in day-to-day life,

   Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. recognise the Islamic manners of walking as part of Islamic ethics.

   Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or on available reference materials the Islamic manners of walking and make notes,

2. demonstrate the Islamic manners of walking, record a short video and share on social media,

3. dramatise the manners to be observed while walking and make a chart distinguishing the positive and negative aspects respectively, learners with visual impairment can be given physical support as they dramatise and make a chart,

4. brainstorm on the significance of Islamic manners of walking in groups and present in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or on available reference materials the Islamic manners of walking and make notes,
2. demonstrate the Islamic manners of walking, record a short video and share on social media,
3. dramatise the manners to be observed while walking and make a chart distinguishing the positive and negative aspects respectively, learners with visual impairment can be given physical support as they dramatise and make a chart,
4. brainstorm on the significance of Islamic manners of walking in groups and present in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Virtues: manners of walking Road safety use together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: the skills of interacting with digital technology and connecting with technology enhanced as learners

search online on the Islamic manners of walking and make notes

● Communication and Collaboration: the skills of listening, speaking, writing and teamwork enhanced as learners brainstorm

on the significance of Islamic manners of walking in groups and present in class

• Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively enhanced as learners dramatise the manners to be observed while

walking and make a chart distinguishing the positive and negative aspects respectively

• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking enhanced as learners dramatise the manners to be observed while

walking and make a chart distinguishing the positive and negative aspects respectively

Values:
• Responsibility: accountability enhanced as learners brainstorm on the significance of Islamic manners of walking in groups

and present in class

• Respect:ettiquette enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinion during group discussions

• Unity: cooperation enhanced as learners brainstorm on the significance of Islamic manners of walking in groups and

present in class

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Safety and security: responsible road use enhanced as learners demonstrate the Islamic manners of walking

Main points to remember:

1. describe the Islamic manners of walking to uphold Islamic teachings,
2. assess the significance of Islamic manners of walking to promote civility,
3. practise the Islamic manners of walking in day-to-day life,
4. recognise the Islamic manners of walking as part of Islamic ethics.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to uphold the Islamic manners of walking?
